stem:
The diagram shows house $H$ and shop $S$ on the same side of straight path $L$. Kavya must walk from $H$ to a point $P$ on $L$, then to $S$, and wants the shortest broken path $H$-$P$-$S$. Point $S'$ is the reflection of $S$ across $L$.

Which claim correctly chooses $P$?

options.text: Take $P$ as the foot of the perpendicular from $H$ to $L$ alone, and ignore $S$ and $S'$.
Call the answer line only, with no choice of $P$ on $L$.
Join $H$ to $S'$ by a straight segment; let $P$ be where that segment meets $L$.
Reflection still chooses $P$ even when $S'$ is not the same distance from $L$ as $S$ is.

teacher.key_rationale: The shortest H-P-S equals the straight path H to S' meeting L at P. A perpendicular from H alone is a different case. Naming only line skips the construction. Dropping equal distance drops the reflection condition.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote grid source into path-line reflection sketch.
